intent.raw_query: Iceland Northern Lights and hot springs, $3500 couple, January 2026

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Located just 20 minutes from Keflavik International Airport, this is an ideal first stop after an early afternoon flight arrival, allowing you to relax and recover from travel before heading to Reykjavik. Book the Comfort package for access to the lagoon, silica mud mask, and use of towels.

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep
experiences.description: Join a small-group super jeep tour departing from central Reykjavik, where expert guides use real-time aurora forecasts to chase the northern lights away from light pollution. Tours typically head toward the Reykjanes Peninsula or Thingvellir area, keeping you close to city-center hotels while maximizing aurora viewing chances. Includes hot chocolate and photography tips.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring pool dating back to 1891 surrounded by geysers and steaming vents. Located in the Golden Circle route, this authentic and less commercialized alternative to the Blue Lagoon pairs perfectly with a Golden Circle day trip. Water stays at a natural 38-40°C year-round, ideal for relaxing under the night sky in winter months.

experiences.name: Thingvellir National Park Aurora Viewing
experiences.description: Drive 45 minutes from Reykjavik to Thingvellir National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site sitting on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge. On clear nights, the park's minimal light pollution makes it one of the best accessible spots near the capital for northern lights photography. During the day, walk between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates. Staying in nearby guesthouses keeps you close to this prime aurora hub.

experiences.name: Fontana Geothermal Baths & Rye Bread Experience
experiences.description: Relax in lakeside geothermal pools at Fontana Spa on the shores of Lake Laugarvatn, where natural steam vents heat the water. Participate in the unique traditional rye bread baking demonstration where bread is baked underground using geothermal heat and served fresh with Icelandic butter. This cultural and hot spring combo is perfectly situated along the Golden Circle, making it easy to combine with other nearby attractions without long detours.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Iceland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and prepare for arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Keflavík International Airport at 13:00. Collect luggage, grab a free map at the tourist information desk, and take the budget-friendly Flybus or shared shuttle (~3,500 ISK) toward South Iceland. Stop at a grocery store (Bónus or Krónan) along the route to stock up on budget essentials — bread, skyr, fruit, instant noodles — to save money throughout the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Check into South Iceland Boutique Stay. Settle in, unpack, and get oriented. Take a short walk around the immediate surroundings as daylight fades (sunset is around 16:30 in January). After dark, step outside or find a dark spot near the accommodation to scan the sky for the Northern Lights — January is peak aurora season in Iceland. Dress in all your layers.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at the airport arrivals hall.
meals.lunch: Pick up a ready-made sandwich or soup from the airport café or a petrol station (N1 or Orkan) — budget ~1,200 ISK.
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal at the accommodation using groceries purchased on the way. Pasta with canned tomato sauce and local skyr for dessert — budget ~800 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: January days in Iceland are very short (~5 hours of daylight). Temperatures average -2°C to 4°C. Layer up with thermal base layers, a windproof jacket, and waterproof boots. Download the Vedur app (Icelandic Met Office) for aurora and weather forecasts. Aurora activity is best after midnight when skies are darkest and clearest.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Seljalandsfoss waterfall, one of Iceland's most iconic falls (~1 hour from most South Iceland accommodations). In January the path behind the waterfall may be icy and closed for safety — check conditions. Admission is free; parking costs ~750 ISK. Enjoy the dramatic frozen landscape and ice formations around the falls in the soft golden winter light (sunrise ~11:00).
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive a short distance to Skógafoss waterfall, another stunning free natural attraction. Climb the staircase alongside the falls for a panoramic view over the South Coast. Explore the base of the falls and look for ice formations. Nearby, visit the free folk museum Skógar Museum if open (small entry fee ~2,000 ISK) to learn about Icelandic heritage.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the accommodation as darkness falls (~16:30). Prepare a warm dinner and then head out for Northern Lights hunting. Drive to a dark rural road away from any light pollution — the flat South Iceland landscape offers wide open skies. Check the aurora forecast on Vedur app (aim for KP index 3+). Bring a thermos of hot chocolate.

meals.breakfast: Oatmeal with skyr and honey made at the accommodation — budget ~400 ISK.
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches and a thermos of soup from the accommodation to eat at Skógafoss — budget ~300 ISK.
meals.dinner: Cook rice and lentil soup with local rye bread at the accommodation — budget ~700 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: Both Seljalandsfoss and Skógafoss are free to visit. Wear microspike crampons or ice grips over your boots — paths are extremely icy in January. Parking fees apply at Seljalandsfoss (~750 ISK). Fuel up the car whenever you pass a petrol station as stations are sparse in rural South Iceland.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the black sand beach of Reynisfjara near Vík — one of Iceland's most dramatic coastal landscapes. See the towering basalt column cliffs (Reynisdrangar), sea stacks, and powerful Atlantic waves. Entry is completely free. Warning: never turn your back on the ocean — sneaker waves are extremely dangerous here. Arrive early to catch the limited winter light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive into the small village of Vík í Mýrdal, the southernmost village in Iceland. Walk up to Vík Church on the hill for panoramic views over the black beach and coastline. Browse the small shops on the main street. Visit the Icelandic Lava Show if budget allows (~4,500 ISK per person) — a unique indoor experience showing live molten lava.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward the accommodation. Stop at a petrol station hot dog stand (N1) for Iceland's famous budget pylsur (hot dogs with all the toppings) — a beloved local tradition at ~600 ISK each. Back at the accommodation, set an alarm for 1:00–3:00 AM and check the aurora forecast for a late-night Northern Lights excursion.

meals.breakfast: Rye bread with local butter and cheese at the accommodation — budget ~350 ISK.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Reynisfjara beach — thermos soup and crackers — budget ~300 ISK.
meals.dinner: Hot dogs at N1 petrol station in Vík (~600 ISK) plus a simple snack back at accommodation.

day_by_day.notes: Reynisfjara is free but extremely dangerous in winter — stay well back from the waterline. Vík is approximately 30–40 minutes east of Seljalandsfoss area. The Lava Show is optional and costs extra but is highly rated as a unique Icelandic experience. Check road conditions at road.is before every drive.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Fjaðrárgljúfur Canyon, a breathtaking and otherworldly river canyon near Kirkjubæjarklaustur. The canyon is about 100 meters deep and 2 km long. Access and parking are free. Walk along the rim trail for dramatic views — the canyon looks especially magical dusted with snow and ice in January. Allow 1.5–2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue east to Kirkjubæjarklaustur village (known locally as 'Klaustur'). Visit the free Systrafoss waterfall and the Systrastapi rock formation. Walk the short trail to Kirkjugólf — a natural basalt column floor formation that looks like a man-made tile floor. All free to visit. Stop at the local petrol station/supermarket to resupply groceries.
day_by_day.evening: Return toward the accommodation. If skies are clear, park on a dark rural road for Northern Lights viewing. The flat, open landscape of South Iceland between Klaustur and Vík is ideal for aurora hunting with minimal light pollution. Bring warm layers and a blanket for the car.

meals.breakfast: Skyr with granola and coffee at the accommodation — budget ~400 ISK.
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch to eat at Fjaðrárgljúfur — rye bread sandwiches and fruit — budget ~350 ISK.
meals.dinner: Cook a budget stew (canned vegetables, potatoes, and lamb) at the accommodation — budget ~900 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: Fjaðrárgljúfur Canyon is about 1 hour east of Vík. Road F206 to the canyon is a gravel road — check if passable in January (may require 4WD). The main Route 1 (Ring Road) is generally well maintained but can be icy. Always check road.is. Kirkjubæjarklaustur has the last fuel station for a long stretch if heading further east.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Skaftafell area within Vatnajökull National Park. Visit the free Svartifoss waterfall — a stunning black basalt column waterfall accessible via a 1.5 km hiking trail from the visitor center. The national park entry is free. The trail may be snowy and icy — wear ice grips. Allow 2–3 hours for the hike.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Skaftafell glacier tongues visible from the park. Walk to the edge of the Skaftafellsjökull glacier for free — you can get very close to the glacier face on a self-guided walk. Do NOT walk onto the glacier without a certified guide. The ice formations and crevasses visible from the safe viewing area are spectacular.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back west toward the accommodation (approximately 1.5–2 hours). Stop at Jökulsárlón glacier lagoon on the way back if time permits — the lagoon glows beautifully under moonlight and aurora. Free to visit. Check aurora forecast and stay for Northern Lights if conditions are favorable.

meals.breakfast: Oatmeal and instant coffee at the accommodation — budget ~350 ISK.
meals.lunch: Packed thermos lunch eaten at Skaftafell visitor center picnic area — budget ~350 ISK.
meals.dinner: Simple pasta with pesto and canned tuna at the accommodation — budget ~750 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: Skaftafell is approximately 1.5–2 hours east of Kirkjubæjarklaustur. Start early to maximize the limited daylight hours. The Skaftafell visitor center has free toilets and information. Vatnajökull National Park entry is completely free. Dress in full winter gear — wind chill is severe near the glacier.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon — one of Iceland's most iconic and magical sights. Icebergs calved from the Breiðamerkurjökull glacier float in the lagoon. Entry and parking are free. Walk along the lagoon shore and watch seals swimming among the icebergs. In January the lagoon may have ice formations and the icebergs can be frozen in place — ethereally beautiful.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 200 meters to Diamond Beach (Breiðársandur) — a black sand beach where translucent icebergs wash ashore, glittering like diamonds. Completely free. Spend time photographing the ice sculptures. Then drive a short distance to Fjallsárlón glacier lagoon — a smaller, quieter lagoon also with stunning glacier views and free access.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward the accommodation. This is one of the best areas in Iceland for Northern Lights due to minimal light pollution and wide open skies. If the aurora forecast is favorable (KP 3+), park at Jökulsárlón or on a dark rural road for aurora viewing. The lights reflecting on the lagoon create a once-in-a-lifetime scene.

meals.breakfast: Rye bread toast with local jam and skyr at accommodation — budget ~350 ISK.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Diamond Beach — sandwiches and hot coffee from thermos — budget ~350 ISK.
meals.dinner: Cook hearty vegetable and barley soup at accommodation — budget ~800 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: Jökulsárlón is approximately 80 km east of Skaftafell. Do not walk on the icebergs or into the lagoon — the water is glacially cold and icebergs can flip without warning. Boat tours are available in summer but not January. The drive back from Jökulsárlón to most South Iceland accommodations is 2.5–3 hours — plan accordingly and drive carefully on potentially icy roads after dark.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day — sleep in and have a leisurely breakfast at the accommodation. Use the morning to do laundry, restock groceries, and plan the second half of the trip. Research free aurora viewing spots near the accommodation and download offline maps.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Lava Centre in Hvolsvöllur (approximately 1 hour from most South Iceland stays) — an interactive exhibition about Iceland's volcanic history. Entry is ~3,900 ISK per person — worth it for a rainy or overcast day. Alternatively, if budget is tight, visit the free Saga Centre nearby which covers the Njáls Saga medieval history.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the area around the accommodation on foot after dark. Look for geothermal hot spring steam vents — South Iceland has many naturally occurring geothermal areas. Some local farms offer access to natural hot pots for free or a small fee (~1,000–2,000 ISK). Ask the accommodation hosts for local tips on secret hot springs.

meals.breakfast: Full cooked breakfast at accommodation — eggs, toast, skyr, coffee — budget ~600 ISK.
meals.lunch: Grocery store run — pick up fresh soup, local bread, and Icelandic dairy products at Bónus or Krónan — budget ~1,200 ISK for restocking.
meals.dinner: Cook lamb soup (kjötsúpa) using local lamb from the supermarket — a classic Icelandic budget meal — budget ~1,000 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: Day 7 is intentionally lighter to allow for rest and flexibility. January weather in Iceland can be unpredictable — use this day as a buffer for weather delays. The Lava Centre is particularly good on a stormy day when outdoor activities are limited. Ask accommodation hosts about local secret hot springs — many South Iceland farms have private geothermal pools not listed online.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Þórsmörk (Thorsmork) Nature Reserve if road conditions permit — check road.is as F-roads require a 4WD super jeep in winter. If accessible, the glacial valley between three glaciers is spectacular in winter snow. Alternatively, hike the lower trails around Mýrdalsjökull glacier visible from Route 1 near Vík for free glacier views without requiring 4WD.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir — one of Iceland's oldest and most affordable geothermal pools (~3,200 ISK entry vs. ~7,000+ ISK at the Blue Lagoon). Soak in the naturally heated outdoor pool (~38–40°C) surrounded by geothermal steam vents and a small geyser. This is a quintessential Icelandic hot spring experience at a fraction of the Blue Lagoon price.
day_by_day.evening: Stay at the Secret Lagoon area until closing or until you're thoroughly warmed through. Drive back to the accommodation under the stars — keep one eye on the sky for Northern Lights. The drive through the interior highlands road (if passable) offers excellent dark sky conditions for aurora spotting.

meals.breakfast: Overnight oats prepared the night before — budget ~350 ISK.
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch for the morning hike — sandwiches, nuts, and dried fruit — budget ~400 ISK.
meals.dinner: Warm up with instant ramen upgraded with a soft-boiled egg and local vegetables at the accommodation — budget ~600 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: The Secret Lagoon in Flúðir is approximately 1–1.5 hours from most South Iceland accommodations. Book online in advance as slots can fill up. Bring your own towel to avoid rental fees (~700 ISK). The pool is open year-round and is particularly magical in winter with steam rising against the dark sky. This is the recommended budget alternative to the Blue Lagoon.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to the Golden Circle — start with Þingvellir (Thingvellir) National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet. Walk through the Almannagjá rift valley for free. This is where Iceland's ancient parliament (Alþingi) was established in 930 AD. The dramatic geology and history make this a must-visit — completely free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Golden Circle to the Geysir Geothermal Area — home of Strokkur geyser which erupts every 5–10 minutes shooting boiling water 20–30 meters into the air. Entry to the geothermal field is completely free. Walk the boardwalk past bubbling mud pools, steaming vents, and colorful mineral deposits. Allow 1–1.5 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Complete the Golden Circle at Gullfoss waterfall — a massive two-tiered waterfall on the Hvítá river. Free entry. In January, the falls may be partially frozen with dramatic ice formations. Walk to the viewing platforms for different perspectives. Drive back to the accommodation — approximately 1.5–2 hours. Check aurora forecast for the drive home.

meals.breakfast: Early start with packed breakfast eaten in the car — granola bars, fruit, and thermos coffee — budget ~400 ISK.
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch to eat at Geysir — the on-site restaurant is expensive, so eat your own food in the car or at outdoor picnic tables — budget ~400 ISK.
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a budget restaurant meal in the Golden Circle area — Lindin Restaurant in Laugarvatn offers affordable Icelandic dishes (~2,500–3,500 ISK per main course) or find a petrol station grill for cheaper options.

day_by_day.notes: The Golden Circle covers approximately 300 km total from South Iceland. Fill up on fuel before leaving. All three main Golden Circle stops (Þingvellir, Geysir, Gullfoss) are free to enter. Avoid the overpriced tourist restaurants at Geysir — bring packed food. Þingvellir is particularly atmospheric in winter with frost and snow. Parking fees may apply at Þingvellir (~750 ISK).

day_by_day.morning: Visit Kerið volcanic crater lake near Selfoss — a stunning red volcanic crater with a vivid blue-green lake at the bottom. Entry fee is ~400 ISK (one of the cheapest paid attractions in Iceland). Walk around the entire crater rim and descend to the lake shore. The contrast of red volcanic rock and turquoise water against winter snow is dramatic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the town of Selfoss — the largest town in South Iceland. Visit the local swimming pool (Selfoss Sundlaug) for a budget hot tub and hot pot experience (~1,000 ISK entry) — Icelandic municipal pools are a fantastic budget alternative to tourist spas. Locals use these pools daily and they always have geothermally heated hot tubs and steam rooms.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to a dark area near the coast south of Selfoss for Northern Lights hunting. The area around Stokkseyri and Eyrarbakki on the south coast has wide open Atlantic views and minimal light pollution — excellent aurora conditions. Walk along the old harbor at Eyrarbakki for a moody winter evening atmosphere. Check Vedur aurora forecast.

meals.breakfast: Skyr with honey and local berries at accommodation — budget ~400 ISK.
meals.lunch: Grab a budget meal at a petrol station in Selfoss — pylsur (hot dog) and a drink for ~800 ISK, or visit the Krónan supermarket for a ready-made meal.
meals.dinner: Cook a simple but satisfying Icelandic-inspired meal at accommodation — pan-fried fish (skrei cod is in season in January) with boiled potatoes and butter — budget ~1,200 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: Kerið crater is a quick 15-minute stop but very photogenic. Selfoss is a practical town for resupplying — has Bónus supermarket, pharmacies, and a gas station. Municipal swimming pools (sundlaugar) are the best budget hot spring experience in Iceland — every town has one and locals use them daily. Bring your own towel and lock for the locker.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Hrunalaug hot spring — a small, free (or donation-based) natural hot spring near Flúðir. This hidden gem is a natural geothermal pool set in a rocky hillside, fitting only about 8–10 people. Arrive early in the morning to avoid crowds (it's become more popular recently). The experience of soaking in a natural hot spring in the Icelandic wilderness is unforgettable.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Haukadalur geothermal valley near Flúðir — walk through the steam vents, bubbling mud pools, and geothermal landscape for free. Visit the small village of Flúðir and its mushroom farm (Sveppabúið) which sells locally grown mushrooms — great for a cheap, fresh dinner ingredient. Stop at the local swimming pool in Flúðir for another hot tub soak (~900 ISK).
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward the accommodation via scenic back roads. Stop at a viewpoint over the Þjórsá river — Iceland's longest river — for sunset/dusk views. After dark, set up for Northern Lights viewing on the flat plains near Þjórsá. The river reflects aurora light beautifully. Bring a tripod if you have one for long-exposure aurora photography.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at accommodation before early departure — toast and peanut butter, coffee — budget ~300 ISK.
meals.lunch: Cook lunch using freshly purchased mushrooms from Flúðir mushroom farm — mushroom omelette or mushroom soup — budget ~600 ISK (bring a portable camp stove or use accommodation).
meals.dinner: Mushroom and potato gratin cooked at accommodation using Flúðir mushrooms — budget ~900 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: Hrunalaug hot spring requires respectful behavior — it is on private land and the landowner allows free/donation access. Leave no trace, do not litter, and be quiet. It can be crowded on weekends — aim for a weekday morning visit. The water temperature varies but is typically around 36–40°C. No facilities — change discreetly.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Þingvellir National Park for a more in-depth exploration. Walk the longer trails through the rift valley in the winter morning light. Visit the Öxará river and Öxárárfoss waterfall within the park — free. Explore the historic Law Rock (Lögberg) where Iceland's ancient parliament convened. The park is magical in winter with frost-covered lava fields and icy rivers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Reykjadalur (Steam Valley) near Hveragerði — a geothermal valley with a naturally heated river you can bathe in for free. The hike to the bathing river is approximately 3 km each way (1–1.5 hours). In January the trail can be icy and snowy — wear proper boots and ice grips. The reward is soaking in a warm river surrounded by snowy mountains and steam vents.
day_by_day.evening: Walk through the small town of Hveragerði — a geothermal town where hot springs bubble up in gardens and greenhouses. Visit the free Earthquake Exhibition in the town center. Have dinner in town or return to the accommodation for a final budget home-cooked meal. Set an alarm for a late-night Northern Lights vigil — one of the last chances of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Porridge with cinnamon and dried fruit at accommodation — budget ~400 ISK.
meals.lunch: Pack a warm thermos lunch for the Reykjadalur hike — instant soup and energy bars — budget ~400 ISK.
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on a sit-down meal in Hveragerði — Kjöt og Kúnst or a local café offers Icelandic lamb soup for ~2,500–3,000 ISK, or cook at home for ~900 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: Reykjadalur is free but requires a moderate winter hike. Check trail conditions — it can be very icy and the trail crosses several streams. Bring a change of clothes and a dry bag for your towel. The hot river temperature varies — test before fully submerging. Hveragerði is approximately 45 minutes from Reykjavík and 1 hour from most South Iceland accommodations. Earthquake Exhibition is free.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — pack up the accommodation and check out. Do a final grocery store run to pick up Icelandic souvenirs on a budget: local skyr, Nói Síríus chocolate, Icelandic sea salt, and dried fish (harðfiskur) — all available cheaply at Bónus or Krónan supermarkets. These make excellent affordable gifts compared to tourist shop prices.
day_by_day.afternoon: If the flight allows time, make a final stop at the Reykjanes Peninsula on the drive back to Keflavík airport. Visit the Bridge Between Continents — a small footbridge spanning the Mid-Atlantic Ridge (free). Drive through the Reykjanes lava fields and stop at Gunnuhver hot spring — a powerful boiling mud pool and steam vent area (free, stay on boardwalks). Return the rental car and check in for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Keflavík International Airport. Reflect on 13 incredible days of Northern Lights, hot springs, glaciers, waterfalls, and volcanic landscapes on a budget. Total estimated accommodation and food costs for the trip: approximately 80,000–110,000 ISK (~€550–€760) excluding flights and car rental.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at accommodation using remaining groceries — clean out the fridge creatively — budget ~400 ISK.
meals.lunch: Petrol station pylsur (hot dogs) near Keflavík — the classic Icelandic farewell meal — budget ~800 ISK.
meals.dinner: Airport meal or food purchased before security — budget ~2,000–3,000 ISK, or eat on the plane.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for car return, shuttle to terminal, and check-in/security. Keflavík airport has free WiFi and comfortable seating. Duty-free at Keflavík sells Icelandic spirits (Brennivín), chocolate, and woolen goods — compare prices to in-town stores. Budget summary: the biggest costs are car rental (~40,000–60,000 ISK for 13 days), fuel (~15,000–20,000 ISK), and accommodation. Food costs kept low by self-catering = approximately 1,000–1,500 ISK per day per person.

trip_options.title: Classic Iceland Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Located just 20 minutes from Keflavik International Airport, this is an ideal first stop after an early afternoon flight arrival, allowing you to relax and recover from travel before heading to Reykjavik. Book the Comfort package for access to the lagoon, silica mud mask, and use of towels.

experiences.name: Thingvellir National Park Aurora Viewing
experiences.description: Drive 45 minutes from Reykjavik to Thingvellir National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site sitting on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge. On clear nights, the park's minimal light pollution makes it one of the best accessible spots near the capital for northern lights photography. During the day, walk between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates. Staying in nearby guesthouses keeps you close to this prime aurora hub.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00. Rest and prepare for arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: Land at Keflavík International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs, collect luggage, and pick up your pre-booked rental car (4WD strongly recommended for January). Drive approximately 20 minutes to the Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa for a late-afternoon soak in the iconic milky-blue geothermal waters. Book the Comfort package in advance — includes silica mud mask, algae mask, and one drink. A perfect way to shake off jet lag and ease into Iceland.
day_by_day.evening: Drive approximately 1.5 hours southeast along Route 1 (Ring Road) to your South Iceland Boutique Stay. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your accommodation. Head into the nearest village for a relaxed first dinner. Keep an eye on the aurora forecast tonight — January skies in South Iceland can offer excellent northern lights visibility away from city light pollution.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or grab a snack at Keflavík Airport (Icelandic lamb soup or a skyr yogurt cup at one of the airport cafés — budget ~1,500–2,000 ISK)
meals.lunch: Light bite at the Blue Lagoon's LAVA Restaurant or the grab-and-go café inside the lagoon facility (soup and bread — ~2,500–3,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Local guesthouse restaurant or a nearby village bistro in South Iceland — try traditional Icelandic lamb stew (kjötsúpa) or pan-fried Arctic char (~3,500–5,000 ISK per person)

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book Blue Lagoon tickets well in advance — January slots sell out quickly. Download the Veðurstofa (Icelandic Met Office) app and the Aurora Forecast app to monitor conditions nightly. Roads may be icy; drive cautiously and check road.is before every journey.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the famous Golden Circle route. Start early (9:00 AM) with a visit to Þingvellir (Thingvellir) National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage Site where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates visibly diverge. Walk the Almannagjá gorge, see Öxará River, and learn about Iceland's ancient parliament (Alþingi). The dramatic landscape is especially moody and beautiful in winter light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Golden Circle to the Geysir Geothermal Area in the Haukadalur Valley. Watch Strokkur geyser erupt every 5–10 minutes shooting water 20–40 meters into the air. Browse the visitor center and geothermal field. Then drive 10 minutes to Gullfoss Waterfall — one of Iceland's most powerful waterfalls, partially frozen in January for a stunning ice-framed spectacle.
day_by_day.evening: Return to South Iceland accommodation (approximately 1.5 hours). After dinner, join a guided Northern Lights tour departing from the South Iceland area, or self-drive to a dark-sky spot along the coast. Thingvellir National Park is also an exceptional aurora viewing location — the same site visited this morning transforms into a magical aurora canvas at night.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic breakfast at your boutique hotel — skyr, rye bread (rúgbrauð), smoked salmon, eggs (~included or ~2,000 ISK if extra)
meals.lunch: Geysir Center café or Gullfoss Café — lamb soup, sandwiches, and hot chocolate to warm up (~2,500–3,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Cozy restaurant near your accommodation — try slow-roasted Icelandic lamb shoulder or fish and chips (~4,000–5,500 ISK per person)

day_by_day.notes: Dress in thermal base layers, mid-layer fleece, and a waterproof outer shell. Waterfall mist freezes on surfaces — wear microspike traction devices. Golden Circle roads are generally well-maintained but check road.is before departing.

day_by_day.morning: Drive the South Coast toward Seljalandsfoss Waterfall (approximately 30 minutes from most South Iceland accommodations). In summer you can walk behind it, but in January enjoy the dramatic frozen curtain of ice from the front. Continue 10 minutes to the hidden gem Gljúfrabúi Waterfall — tucked inside a narrow canyon, partially accessible even in winter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue east to Skógafoss Waterfall — one of Iceland's largest and most photogenic waterfalls. Climb the staircase beside it (if ice conditions permit) for sweeping views over the South Coast. Then drive further east to the black sand beach at Reynisfjara near Vík — admire the dramatic basalt column formations (Reynisdrangar sea stacks) and powerful Atlantic surf. Do NOT approach the waves — sneaker waves are extremely dangerous year-round.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the charming village of Vík í Mýrdal — Iceland's southernmost village. Enjoy dinner here, then return to your accommodation. Tonight, check aurora forecasts and if KP index is 3+, drive to a dark coastal spot for potential northern lights viewing over the black sand beach — a truly unforgettable combination.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or pack a thermos of coffee and grab pastries from a local bakery before departing
meals.lunch: Black Beach Restaurant in Vík or Suður-Vík restaurant — fish soup and fresh bread with ocean views (~3,000–4,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Halldórskaffi in Vík — a beloved local restaurant serving traditional Icelandic dishes including lamb and fresh fish (~4,000–5,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: January daylight in Iceland is very limited (roughly 5–6 hours, approximately 11:00 AM–4:30 PM). Plan outdoor sightseeing during these hours and embrace the long dark evenings for aurora hunting. Reynisfjara beach warning signs must be respected — fatalities occur regularly from rogue waves.

day_by_day.morning: Drive east toward Mýrdalsjökull Glacier area. Stop at the Dyrhólaey promontory (if accessible — check locally, as it sometimes closes in winter) for panoramic views of the black sand coastline and the famous rock arch. Continue toward the Eldhraun lava field — one of the world's largest lava fields, covered in soft green moss, eerily beautiful in winter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Fjaðrárgljúfur Canyon — a stunning 100-meter-deep, 2-kilometer-long canyon carved by glacial meltwater. The canyon walls are layered with basalt and draped in moss. In January, the canyon may be partially snow-dusted, creating a dramatic winter scene. Then stop at the small town of Kirkjubæjarklaustur for a warm break.
day_by_day.evening: Return toward your South Iceland base or stay in the Kirkjubæjarklaustur area if you've extended your range. Enjoy a quiet evening with a home-cooked-style meal at a local guesthouse. Spend the late evening on an aurora watch — the eastern South Coast has remarkably dark skies with minimal light pollution.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — fuel up well before a long driving day
meals.lunch: Systrakaffi in Kirkjubæjarklaustur — a beloved community café serving homemade soups, sandwiches, and legendary cakes (~2,500–3,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Guesthouse restaurant in Kirkjubæjarklaustur or pack a simple self-catered dinner from a local supermarket (Krónan or Bónus) — budget-friendly option (~1,500–2,500 ISK self-catered)

day_by_day.notes: Fjaðrárgljúfur Canyon access can be restricted in winter — verify locally before visiting. The road to Dyrhólaey (Route 218) may be icy or closed; always check road.is. Fuel up your car whenever you see a petrol station in rural Iceland — stations can be far apart.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Skaftafell, part of Vatnajökull National Park — Europe's largest national park. Take a leisurely winter walk to Svartifoss Waterfall, framed by stunning hexagonal basalt columns draped in ice. The park visitor center offers excellent exhibits on glaciers, volcanoes, and Icelandic geology.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a guided glacier walk or ice cave tour on Vatnajökull Glacier — the largest glacier in Europe. January is prime season for visiting the famous crystal blue ice caves inside the glacier. Book a reputable certified guide (such as Local Guide or Glacier Guides) — this is a non-negotiable safety requirement. The electric blue ice formations are among the most extraordinary natural spectacles on Earth.
day_by_day.evening: Return from the glacier tour (tours typically end by 4:00–5:00 PM in winter). Drive back west along the Ring Road toward your accommodation. Dinner at your hotel or a nearby restaurant. Tonight is another excellent opportunity for northern lights — the vast flat plains of South Iceland offer 360-degree sky views.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast — glacier tours often depart at 9:00–10:00 AM
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch or eat at the Skaftafell Visitor Center café before the glacier tour (~2,000–3,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Restaurant at or near your South Iceland boutique accommodation — treat yourself to pan-seared skyr-marinated lamb or Icelandic beef (~5,000–6,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Ice cave tours MUST be booked in advance — they sell out weeks ahead in January. Budget approximately 15,000–20,000 ISK per person for a guided glacier/ice cave experience. All equipment (crampons, helmets) is provided by the guide company. Never enter ice caves without a certified guide.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon — one of Iceland's most iconic and breathtaking landscapes. Watch enormous icebergs calved from Breiðamerkurjökull Glacier float slowly across the lagoon toward the sea. In January, the lagoon may be partially frozen, creating a surreal silent landscape. Seals are frequently spotted resting on the ice floes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 200 meters from Jökulsárlón to Diamond Beach — where translucent ice chunks wash ashore on black volcanic sand, glittering like scattered diamonds. Spend time photographing this magical scene (it's a photographer's dream). Then drive back west along the Ring Road, stopping at the Núpsstaðarskógar forest — one of Iceland's rare natural woodlands, enchanting in winter.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back at your South Iceland accommodation. Enjoy a relaxing evening — consider booking a private hot tub session at your boutique hotel if available, or visit a nearby geothermal pool (many South Iceland towns have community swimming pools with hot pots open year-round). Check aurora forecast for a potential late-night lights show.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — pack snacks for the road (Jökulsárlón is a long drive from central South Iceland)
meals.lunch: Glacier Goose Café at Jökulsárlón — the only food option nearby, serving lamb soup, hot drinks, and waffles (~2,500–3,500 ISK). Arrive early as it gets busy.
meals.dinner: Return to hotel restaurant or nearby South Iceland dining — try Icelandic langoustine (lobster) soup, a regional specialty (~4,500–6,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Jökulsárlón is approximately 1.5–2 hours east of Vík. Allow a full day for this excursion. The road can be challenging in winter — 4WD essential. Boat tours on the lagoon do not operate in January (frozen conditions), but the walking experience is exceptional. Keep a safe distance from icebergs on Diamond Beach — they can roll unexpectedly.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day — a mid-trip slower pace is intentional for a balanced itinerary. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast, and take a slow morning walk near your accommodation. South Iceland's countryside is stunning even on a quiet wander — look for Icelandic horses in the fields, steam rising from geothermal vents, and the distant silhouettes of glaciers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local geothermal swimming pool — nearly every Icelandic town has one and they are central to daily life. The pools are heated by natural geothermal energy and include hot pots at various temperatures (typically 38–44°C). This is where locals unwind and socialize. Entry is typically 1,000–1,500 ISK — exceptional value. Alternatively, explore the nearby Hvolsvöllur area and the Saga Centre museum dedicated to Njáls Saga.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a special mid-trip dinner at a slightly elevated restaurant — splurge modestly on a tasting menu or chef's special featuring local ingredients. Spend the evening aurora hunting with a warm flask of hot chocolate, ideally parked at a dark coastal location or near a mountain backdrop for dramatic silhouette photos.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast — take your time
meals.lunch: Local bakery or café — fresh-baked Icelandic cinnamon rolls (snúðar), skyr with granola, and coffee (~1,500–2,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Slightly elevated dinner at a regional restaurant — 2-course meal with local lamb or fish as centerpiece (~5,500–7,500 ISK per person with a glass of Icelandic craft beer)

day_by_day.notes: This rest day is important — Iceland travel involves a lot of driving on challenging roads. Recharging physically and mentally ensures you enjoy the second half of the trip fully. Use this afternoon to review upcoming days, reconfirm bookings, and charge all camera batteries and power banks.

day_by_day.morning: Drive toward the Westman Islands (Vestmannaeyjar) ferry terminal at Landeyjahöfn (approximately 30 minutes from central South Iceland). Take the Herjólfur ferry to Heimaey — the only inhabited island of the Westman Islands archipelago. The 35-minute ferry crossing offers views of dramatic sea cliffs and seabird colonies (puffins return in spring, but the cliffs are impressive year-round). Note: Check ferry schedule and weather conditions — winter crossings can be cancelled in rough seas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Heimaey Island. Visit the Eldheimar Museum — a world-class museum built around a house buried by the 1973 Eldfell volcanic eruption. The museum tells the extraordinary story of the overnight evacuation of the entire island population. Walk up Eldfell Volcano for panoramic views (approximately 45-minute hike). The ground near the summit is still warm from residual geothermal heat.
day_by_day.evening: Take the late afternoon/early evening ferry back to the mainland (check return schedule carefully — last ferry times vary seasonally). Drive back to your South Iceland accommodation for dinner. The Westman Islands day trip is one of South Iceland's most rewarding and often-overlooked experiences.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before ferry departure
meals.lunch: Gott restaurant in Heimaey — one of the island's best restaurants, serving fresh local seafood including puffin (a controversial but traditional Icelandic dish) and langoustine (~3,500–5,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Hotel restaurant or local South Iceland eatery upon return — something simple and warming after a full day (~3,500–4,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Ferry tickets should be booked in advance at seatours.is or herjolfur.is. The Westman Islands ferry can be cancelled in winter storms — have a flexible backup plan. Heimaey is a small, walkable island — no car rental needed for a day trip. Dress for strong coastal winds.

day_by_day.morning: Drive west toward Reykjavik (approximately 1.5–2 hours from South Iceland). Arrive in Iceland's capital and begin exploring. Start at Hallgrímskirkja Church — the iconic 73-meter concrete church modeled after basalt lava columns. Take the elevator to the tower observation deck for panoramic city views. Walk down Skólavörðustígur street lined with colorful boutiques and cafés.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Harpa Concert Hall on the harbor — a stunning glass facade building that changes color with the light. Walk along the old harbor waterfront (Grandi area) and visit the Whales of Iceland exhibition — life-size models of 23 whale species found in Icelandic waters, beautifully presented. Browse the Kolaportið flea market (open Saturdays and Sundays) for local crafts, vintage items, and traditional Icelandic food.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Reykjavik's vibrant Laugavegur street for dinner and evening atmosphere. The city has excellent mid-range dining options. After dinner, join a Northern Lights bus tour departing from Reykjavik — tour operators monitor conditions in real time and drive to the best viewing locations outside the city. Most tours offer a free rebooking if lights don't appear.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departing South Iceland, or stop at a café in Selfoss town en route
meals.lunch: Reykjavik Roasters café or Bergsson Mathús — excellent coffee, fresh sourdough sandwiches, and Icelandic open-faced smørrebrød (~2,500–3,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Messinn Restaurant on Laugavegur — famous for their cast-iron skillets of fresh Icelandic fish served with butter sauce and potatoes (~5,000–7,000 ISK per person)

day_by_day.notes: Parking in Reykjavik requires payment in designated zones (use the Parka app). Consider staying in Reykjavik tonight if your boutique hotel allows flexibility, or plan the drive back to South Iceland after the aurora tour (approximately midnight return). Northern lights tours from Reykjavik cost approximately 8,000–12,000 ISK per person.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a second morning in Reykjavik. Visit the National Museum of Iceland (Þjóðminjasafn Íslands) — a superb museum covering 1,200 years of Icelandic history from the Viking settlement to modern times. Entry approximately 2,500 ISK. Then visit the Settlement Exhibition (Landnámssýningin) — built around a Viking longhouse excavated beneath the city streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive 45 minutes from Reykjavik to Thingvellir National Park for a dedicated aurora viewing preparation visit. In daylight, explore the continental rift valley, Öxará River, and the historic Law Rock (Lögberg). Understand the landscape so that when you return in darkness for aurora viewing, you know the terrain. Alternatively, visit the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) near Flúðir — Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a more authentic and less crowded hot spring experience than the Blue Lagoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Thingvellir National Park after dark for the Thingvellir Aurora Viewing experience. The park sits on the tectonic plate boundary with virtually zero light pollution. On a clear night with KP index 3+, the northern lights dance directly over the rift valley — an extraordinary and deeply moving experience. Bring a tripod for long-exposure photography.

meals.breakfast: Reykjavik café breakfast — try Brauð & Co bakery for Iceland's most celebrated cinnamon rolls and pastries (~1,500–2,000 ISK)
meals.lunch: Café at Thingvellir National Park visitor center — soup and sandwiches (~2,500–3,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Pack a thermos of hot soup and sandwiches for the aurora viewing session, or eat at a Reykjavik restaurant before heading to Thingvellir (~3,500–5,000 ISK at a Reykjavik restaurant)

day_by_day.notes: The Secret Lagoon costs approximately 3,500 ISK per person — book online in advance. Thingvellir aurora viewing is self-guided and free. The park has designated parking areas and walking paths safe to use in darkness. Dress extremely warmly for standing still in January temperatures — layering is critical. Hand warmers are highly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Drive the Snæfellsnes Peninsula (approximately 2 hours northwest of Reykjavik) — often called 'Iceland in Miniature' for its concentration of diverse landscapes. Begin at Kirkjufell Mountain — Iceland's most photographed mountain, shaped like a perfect arrowhead. The adjacent Kirkjufellsfoss waterfall creates a classic composition. In winter, the mountain may be snow-capped and the falls partially frozen.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue around the peninsula to Snæfellsjökull Glacier and National Park — the mystical glacier volcano immortalized in Jules Verne's 'Journey to the Center of the Earth.' Visit Djúpalónssandur black pebble beach with its dramatic lava formations and shipwreck remains. Explore the Vatnshellir lava tube cave (guided tours available, approximately 3,000 ISK) and the Arnarstapi coastal cliffs.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward South Iceland or stay in the Snæfellsnes/West Iceland area if preferred. If returning south, stop for dinner in Borgarnes — a pleasant town with excellent restaurants. Arrive at accommodation by 9:00–10:00 PM. Check aurora forecast — the drive back through rural West Iceland passes through exceptionally dark sky territory.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before the long drive to Snæfellsnes
meals.lunch: Fjöruhúsið café at Hellnar — a legendary cliffside café serving fish soup and cakes with ocean views, one of Iceland's most beloved lunch spots (~3,000–4,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Borgarnes Settlement Center restaurant or Hyrnan restaurant in Borgarnes — excellent lamb and fish dishes (~4,000–5,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Snæfellsnes is a long day trip (approximately 300–350 km round trip from South Iceland). Consider an overnight in Snæfellsnes/Borgarnes to reduce driving pressure. The peninsula road is generally well-maintained but can be icy — 4WD essential. Vatnshellir cave tours depart at set times; check schedule at the park visitor center.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day — return to any favorite locations for a second visit or explore areas not yet covered. Consider revisiting the South Coast in the morning light — the Mýrdalsjökull Glacier area and Eyjafjallajökull Volcano (famous from the 2010 eruption) are beautiful in clear winter conditions. Visit the Þórsmörk (Thorsmork) mountain reserve if road conditions permit — a dramatic glacial valley between three glaciers accessible by super-jeep.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local geothermal bakery to try hverabrauð (hot spring rye bread) — traditionally baked underground using geothermal heat for 24 hours. The Laugarvatn Fontana Geothermal Baths offer this experience along with beautiful lakeside hot spring pools — a more intimate and authentic alternative to the Blue Lagoon. Laugarvatn is conveniently located on the Golden Circle route (~45 minutes from South Iceland).
day_by_day.evening: Final aurora viewing attempt — this is your last dedicated night for northern lights hunting. Drive to the darkest accessible location near your accommodation. If the trip has been cloudy, tonight may be the night. Celebrate your Iceland adventure with a special farewell dinner featuring the best of Icelandic cuisine — skyr dessert, lamb, Arctic char, and a glass of Brennivín (Icelandic schnapps, nicknamed 'Black Death') as a traditional send-off.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast — savor the last full morning
meals.lunch: Laugarvatn Fontana café — fresh hverabrauð rye bread with Icelandic butter and smoked trout, eaten lakeside (~2,500–3,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at your South Iceland boutique hotel restaurant or the best local restaurant — 3-course meal with Icelandic lamb, fresh fish, and skyr dessert with crowberries (~6,000–8,500 ISK per person)

day_by_day.notes: Laugarvatn Fontana entry costs approximately 4,500–5,500 ISK per person including access to all pools and steam rooms. The hverabrauð experience is included. Book in advance during peak season. Þórsmörk by super-jeep costs approximately 15,000–20,000 ISK per person if joining a guided tour — only accessible with specialized vehicles in winter.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — check out of South Iceland Boutique Stay. Pack carefully, ensuring all gear is accounted for. Take a final slow drive through the South Iceland landscape, stopping for one last photo of the glaciers, waterfalls, and Icelandic horses before heading toward Keflavík. Stop in Selfoss or Hveragerði for a last Icelandic coffee and pastry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Keflavík International Airport with ample time (recommend arriving 2.5–3 hours before departure for international flights). Return your rental car. Browse the airport's excellent duty-free selection — Icelandic wool products (lopapeysa sweaters), Icelandic sea salt, skyr chocolate, and Brennivín make excellent souvenirs. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days in Iceland.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Keflavík International Airport. Carry the memories of geothermal waters, dancing northern lights, glacier ice caves, volcanic landscapes, and the profound silence of Iceland's winter wilderness.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or grab skyr and a pastry at a Hveragerði café on the drive to the airport (~1,500–2,000 ISK)
meals.lunch: Keflavík Airport restaurants — Fiskmarkaðurinn (Fish Market) airport branch or Einars Mathús for a final Icelandic fish dish (~3,500–5,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Onboard flight meal or airport dining depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Allow extra time for car return (budget 45–60 minutes for fuel top-up, car inspection, and shuttle to terminal). January weather can cause flight delays — monitor your flight status. Keflavík Airport has a lovely Blue Lagoon-branded spa airside if you have a long layover. Keep one layer of warm clothing accessible in your carry-on in case of weather delays. Góða ferð — safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Iceland Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Located just 20 minutes from Keflavik International Airport, this is an ideal first stop after an early afternoon flight arrival, allowing you to relax and recover from travel before heading to Reykjavik. Book the Comfort package for access to the lagoon, silica mud mask, and use of towels.

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep
experiences.description: Join a small-group super jeep tour departing from central Reykjavik, where expert guides use real-time aurora forecasts to chase the northern lights away from light pollution. Tours typically head toward the Reykjanes Peninsula or Thingvellir area, keeping you close to city-center hotels while maximizing aurora viewing chances. Includes hot chocolate and photography tips.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring pool dating back to 1891 surrounded by geysers and steaming vents. Located in the Golden Circle route, this authentic and less commercialized alternative to the Blue Lagoon pairs perfectly with a Golden Circle day trip. Water stays at a natural 38-40°C year-round, ideal for relaxing under the night sky in winter months.

experiences.name: Thingvellir National Park Aurora Viewing
experiences.description: Drive 45 minutes from Reykjavik to Thingvellir National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site sitting on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge. On clear nights, the park's minimal light pollution makes it one of the best accessible spots near the capital for northern lights photography. During the day, walk between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates. Staying in nearby guesthouses keeps you close to this prime aurora hub.

experiences.name: Fontana Geothermal Baths & Rye Bread Experience
experiences.description: Relax in lakeside geothermal pools at Fontana Spa on the shores of Lake Laugarvatn, where natural steam vents heat the water. Participate in the unique traditional rye bread baking demonstration where bread is baked underground using geothermal heat and served fresh with Icelandic butter. This cultural and hot spring combo is perfectly situated along the Golden Circle, making it easy to combine with other nearby attractions without long detours.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Keflavik International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and meet your pre-arranged private luxury transfer driver.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private chauffeur transfer from Keflavik Airport directly to the Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa (en route to South Iceland). Pre-booked Premium or Retreat Spa package includes access to the iconic milky-blue geothermal waters, silica mud mask, algae mask, in-water massage bar, and a welcome drink. Spend 2–3 hours unwinding after your flight.
day_by_day.evening: Continue private transfer to your South Iceland Boutique Stay. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your luxury suite. Enjoy a welcome dinner at the hotel's fine dining restaurant or a recommended nearby restaurant such as Rauða Húsið (The Red House) in Eyrarbakki, known for langoustine and locally sourced Icelandic cuisine.

meals.breakfast: On the flight or at Keflavik Airport's Aurora Restaurant lounge (pre-arrival)
meals.lunch: Light refreshments and a welcome drink included at the Blue Lagoon Retreat Spa
meals.dinner: Rauða Húsið (The Red House), Eyrarbakki — celebrated Icelandic langoustine soup, pan-seared Arctic char, and local lamb with Icelandic wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book Blue Lagoon Retreat package well in advance — slots fill up months ahead. Ensure your private transfer is confirmed before departure. January sunset in Iceland is around 16:30, so the Blue Lagoon experience will transition beautifully into a twilight and evening soak.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely breakfast at your South Iceland Boutique Stay. Depart mid-morning to explore the iconic Golden Circle route. Begin at Þingvellir (Thingvellir) National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage Site where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet. Walk the Almannagjá rift valley with a private guide who explains the geological and historical significance of Iceland's ancient parliament site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Golden Circle to the Geysir Geothermal Area to witness Strokkur erupting every 5–10 minutes. Then visit the majestic Gullfoss waterfall, dramatic even in winter with ice formations framing the cascading glacial water. Stop at Fontana Geothermal Baths on Lake Laugarvatn for the signature experience: soak in lakeside geothermal pools and enjoy the unique rye bread (hverabrauð) baked underground in the hot springs, served with Icelandic butter.
day_by_day.evening: Return to South Iceland Boutique Stay. After dark, your hotel concierge monitors aurora forecasts. If KP index is favorable (KP 3+), embark on a private Northern Lights viewing excursion from the hotel grounds or a nearby dark-sky location. South Iceland's low light pollution makes it ideal for aurora hunting.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic breakfast at the boutique hotel — skyr parfait, smoked salmon, rye bread, Icelandic lamb sausage, and freshly brewed coffee
meals.lunch: Café Laugarvatn or Fontana Spa's café — traditional Icelandic lamb soup (kjötsúpa), geothermal rye bread with smoked trout, and hot cocoa
meals.dinner: Hotel fine dining or Friðheimar Tomato Farm Restaurant (Golden Circle area) — unique greenhouse dining with tomato-based menu, fresh pasta, and Bloody Mary cocktails made from house-grown tomatoes

day_by_day.notes: January days are short (sunrise ~11:00, sunset ~16:30). Plan Golden Circle stops efficiently. Fontana's rye bread experience should be booked as part of the spa visit. Dress in thermal layers — temperatures can be -5°C to 0°C with wind chill.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, take a guided private tour of the South Coast highlights. Begin at Seljalandsfoss waterfall — in winter, the surrounding ice formations create a breathtaking scene. Walk behind the falls (conditions permitting in January) with crampons provided by your guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Skógafoss waterfall, one of Iceland's largest and most dramatic. If conditions allow, hike the icy steps to the viewing platform above for panoramic views of the South Coast. Proceed to the black sand beach at Reynisfjara near Vík — dramatic basalt column formations, sea stacks (Reynisdrangar), and powerful Atlantic waves create an otherworldly landscape. Visit the charming village of Vík.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your boutique stay. Evening aurora watch from the hotel or a pre-arranged private dark-sky location with your guide. Warm up afterward with a private in-room hot tub session if available at your accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — Icelandic pancakes (pönnukökur) with cream and jam, smoked lamb, fresh fruit, and Icelandic dairy
meals.lunch: Skool Beans café in Vík or a premium packed gourmet lunch prepared by the hotel — artisan sandwiches with smoked Icelandic lamb, local cheeses, and thermos of lamb soup
meals.dinner: Suður-Vík Restaurant in Vík — cozy intimate dining with lamb fillet, fresh fish of the day, and Icelandic craft beer or wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Black sand beaches like Reynisfjara are extremely dangerous due to sneaker waves. Never turn your back to the ocean. Your private guide will brief you on safety. Crampons are essential for icy waterfall paths in January.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, embark on a private glacier experience at Sólheimajökull glacier (outlet glacier of Mýrdalsjökull). Equipped with crampons, ice axes, and harnesses, explore the dramatic blue ice caves, crevasses, and glacier formations with a certified glacier guide. This is a world-class glaciological experience unique to Iceland.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon — one of Iceland's most iconic sights. Watch enormous icebergs calved from Breiðamerkurjökull glacier float serenely in the lagoon. In January, the lagoon may be partially frozen, adding to the ethereal atmosphere. Walk to Diamond Beach (Breiðamerkursandur) where crystal-clear ice blocks wash ashore on black sand.
day_by_day.evening: Overnight at a pre-arranged luxury accommodation near Jökulsárlón or return toward South Iceland base. If staying near the lagoon area, this remote location offers exceptional dark skies for Northern Lights viewing. Arrange a private aurora alert service with your guide.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast before early departure
meals.lunch: Glacier Goose Café near Jökulsárlón (seasonal) or a premium hotel-prepared gourmet packed lunch with hot soup thermos, smoked fish, and artisan bread
meals.dinner: Hali Country Hotel Restaurant near Jökulsárlón — farm-to-table Icelandic cuisine, reindeer, lamb, and locally caught fish with panoramic glacier views

day_by_day.notes: Jökulsárlón is approximately 2.5 hours from the South Iceland base — an early start is recommended. The glacier walk requires moderate fitness. All safety equipment is provided. January temperatures near the glacier can drop to -10°C — dress in expedition-grade thermal layers.

day_by_day.morning: Return journey westward along the Ring Road. Stop at Fjaðrárgljúfur Canyon — a stunning 100-meter deep, 2 km long canyon carved by glacial meltwater. In winter, the canyon walls may be draped in ice and snow, creating a surreal landscape. A short walk along the rim offers spectacular views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir — Iceland's oldest swimming pool dating to 1891. Soak in the naturally heated geothermal pool (38–40°C) surrounded by geysers and hot spring activity. The rustic, authentic atmosphere contrasts beautifully with the Blue Lagoon experience. Small, intimate, and far less crowded — a true hidden gem.
day_by_day.evening: Return to South Iceland Boutique Stay. Enjoy a relaxing evening with an in-hotel spa treatment or private hot tub session. If aurora forecast is strong, arrange a short private drive to a dark-sky spot with your guide.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at overnight accommodation near Jökulsárlón or en route café
meals.lunch: Kaffi Langabúð in Kirkjubæjarklaustur — homemade Icelandic soups, fresh bread, and coffee in a charming historic building
meals.dinner: Hotel fine dining at South Iceland Boutique Stay — tasting menu featuring Icelandic lamb, Arctic char, langoustine, and seasonal foraged ingredients with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Fjaðrárgljúfur Canyon access may be restricted in winter — confirm with your guide before visiting. The Secret Lagoon is best visited in late afternoon as darkness falls for a magical stargazing experience while soaking. Book in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated relaxation morning at your South Iceland Boutique Stay. Enjoy a late breakfast, spa treatments, and leisure time. Alternatively, take a guided horseback riding experience on Icelandic horses — a unique breed known for the smooth 'tölt' gait. Ride through snow-covered lava fields and countryside for a truly Icelandic experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Kerið volcanic crater — a 3,000-year-old explosion crater with a vivid turquoise lake at the bottom. In winter, the lake may be frozen and snow-covered, making it even more dramatic. Continue to Hveragerði, Iceland's geothermal garden town, where hot springs bubble up through gardens and greenhouses. Walk the geothermal river valley (Reykjadalur) if conditions permit.
day_by_day.evening: Private Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep departing from the South Iceland area. Expert guides use real-time aurora forecasting, satellite data, and cloud cover mapping to chase the optimal viewing location. The super jeep's 4WD capability allows access to remote dark-sky highland locations inaccessible by standard vehicles.

meals.breakfast: Extended luxury breakfast at hotel — full Icelandic spread with skyr, smoked fish, lamb, fresh pastries, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Ölverk Pizza & Brewery in Hveragerði — craft beer brewed with geothermal energy, artisan pizzas with Icelandic toppings (lamb, smoked fish, local cheeses)
meals.dinner: Pre-packed gourmet dinner in the super jeep during the aurora hunt, or late dinner at hotel upon return — warm lamb stew, artisan bread, and Icelandic schnapps (brennivín)

day_by_day.notes: The Super Jeep Northern Lights tour is weather-dependent. Your guide will confirm departure based on aurora and cloud cover forecasts. Dress in your warmest expedition gear — standing outside in -5°C to -15°C wind chill while watching auroras requires serious insulation.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Reykjavik. Private luxury transfer to Iceland's capital. Begin with a guided walking tour of the city's highlights: Hallgrímskirkja church (take the elevator to the tower for panoramic city views), Harpa Concert Hall (stunning geometric glass architecture), and the historic Tjörnin pond area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Reykjavik's world-class culinary and cultural scene. Visit the Reykjavik Art Museum or the National Museum of Iceland for cultural context. Browse the boutique shops on Laugavegur street for premium Icelandic wool products (lopapeysa sweaters), design items, and local crafts. Visit a premium spa such as Sky Lagoon for cliff-top ocean views while soaking in geothermal seawater.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at one of Reykjavik's top fine dining restaurants. Afterward, if aurora forecast permits, join the Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep departing from central Reykjavik — guides will drive to optimal viewing locations outside the city. Alternatively, return to South Iceland for a private aurora watch.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Grillmarkaðurinn (The Grill Market), Reykjavik — premium Icelandic steakhouse with dry-aged lamb, lobster, and Arctic char; one of Iceland's most celebrated restaurants
meals.dinner: Dill Restaurant, Reykjavik — Iceland's first Michelin-starred restaurant; Nordic New Wave cuisine featuring hyper-local, foraged, and fermented Icelandic ingredients with exceptional wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Reserve Dill Restaurant well in advance — it is one of the most sought-after dining reservations in Iceland. Sky Lagoon should also be pre-booked. The drive from South Iceland to Reykjavik is approximately 1 hour via Route 1.

day_by_day.morning: Snowmobile adventure on Langjökull glacier — Iceland's second-largest glacier. A private transfer takes you to the glacier where you'll ride snowmobiles across the vast white expanse with panoramic views of the Icelandic highlands. An exhilarating, bucket-list experience unique to Iceland's winter landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Into the Glacier tunnel system inside Langjökull — a man-made tunnel system carved into the glacier itself, revealing blue ice walls, ice caves, and a glacier chapel. A guided tour explains glaciology and climate change impacts on Iceland's ice caps.
day_by_day.evening: Return to South Iceland Boutique Stay. Luxurious recovery evening — book an in-hotel massage or hot stone therapy treatment. Soak in the hotel's private hot tub under the stars. Monitor aurora forecasts and step outside if conditions are favorable.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — early departure required for glacier activities
meals.lunch: Packed premium gourmet lunch on the glacier provided by the tour operator — hot soup, smoked lamb sandwiches, Icelandic chocolate, and hot drinks
meals.dinner: Intimate hotel dinner — slow-roasted Icelandic lamb shoulder, root vegetable gratin, skyr panna cotta, and Icelandic craft spirits

day_by_day.notes: Langjökull snowmobile and glacier tunnel tours require advance booking through a specialist operator. Warm, waterproof outer layers and goggles are provided, but thermal base layers are essential. The glacier is approximately 1.5–2 hours from South Iceland.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated aurora recovery and leisure morning. Sleep in, enjoy a late breakfast, and spend time in the hotel's relaxation areas. Optional: gentle yoga session or guided meditation arranged by the hotel in a room with panoramic Icelandic landscape views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided tour of the Westman Islands (Vestmannaeyjar) via ferry from Landeyjahöfn (30-minute crossing) or private helicopter transfer for the ultimate luxury experience. Explore the volcanic archipelago formed by one of Iceland's most recent eruptions (Eldfell, 1973). Visit the Eldheimar Museum — a preserved house buried by the 1973 lava flow, Iceland's 'Pompeii.'
day_by_day.evening: Return to South Iceland. Thingvellir National Park Aurora Viewing — private evening excursion to Þingvellir, one of Iceland's darkest and most atmospheric locations for aurora hunting. The UNESCO site's dramatic rift valley provides a stunning foreground for aurora photography.

meals.breakfast: Extended hotel breakfast — full Icelandic spread
meals.lunch: Einsi Kaldi Restaurant in Vestmannaeyjar — fresh seafood, locally caught fish, and Westman Islands specialty dishes
meals.dinner: Hotel fine dining — langoustine bisque, pan-seared cod with dill butter, and Icelandic blueberry skyr dessert with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Check ferry schedules from Landeyjahöfn in advance — winter sailings may be reduced. Helicopter transfer to Westman Islands is a premium add-on that must be arranged through a specialist operator. Þingvellir aurora viewing is best on clear, moonless nights.

day_by_day.morning: Ice cave exploration in the Vatnajökull area — one of Iceland's most extraordinary winter-only experiences. Natural ice caves form each winter inside the glacier, featuring cathedral-like chambers of vivid blue, turquoise, and crystal ice. A private certified guide leads a small exclusive group through these ephemeral wonders.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Skaftá river area and the vast Eldhraun lava field — the largest lava flow in recorded human history (1783 Laki eruption), now covered in a soft carpet of moss. Drive through this otherworldly landscape with your private guide explaining Iceland's volcanic geology.
day_by_day.evening: Return to South Iceland Boutique Stay. Private stargazing session arranged by the hotel — a local astronomer joins you with a high-powered telescope to observe Iceland's exceptionally clear winter skies. If aurora activity is present, the evening transforms into a dual stargazing and Northern Lights experience.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before glacier departure
meals.lunch: Hot packed lunch on the glacier tour — lamb soup in thermos, smoked fish, rye bread, and Icelandic chocolate
meals.dinner: Hótel Rangá Restaurant (nearby luxury hotel restaurant) — one of South Iceland's finest dining venues, known for wild game, reindeer, and exceptional Icelandic ingredients with panoramic Hekla volcano views

day_by_day.notes: Natural ice caves are only accessible November through March and vary year to year based on glacial conditions. Booking through a certified glacier guide operator is mandatory. Hótel Rangá is also renowned as one of Iceland's premier Northern Lights viewing hotels — their aurora wake-up call service is legendary.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Landmannalaugar area (accessible by super jeep in winter) — Iceland's famous highland geothermal area known for colorful rhyolite mountains and natural hot spring pools. Soak in the natural geothermal river pool surrounded by snow-covered volcanic mountains — one of Iceland's most remote and spectacular hot spring experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Þórsmörk (Thorsmork) nature reserve by super jeep — a stunning glacial valley surrounded by three glaciers (Eyjafjallajökull, Mýrdalsjökull, and Tindfjallajökull). Walk through birch forests and river valleys with your guide. The landscape feels like the end of the world in winter.
day_by_day.evening: Return to South Iceland Boutique Stay. Final dedicated Northern Lights Hunt evening — arrange a private aurora photography session with a professional photographer who will guide you in capturing long-exposure aurora images as a lasting memory of your trip.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — energy-rich meal before a full highland day
meals.lunch: Packed premium gourmet lunch in the super jeep — hot lamb soup, artisan sandwiches, Icelandic energy bars, and hot chocolate
meals.dinner: Farewell-eve dinner at South Iceland Boutique Stay — chef's special tasting menu celebrating Icelandic terroir: langoustine, lamb, Arctic char, skyr, and foraged berries with premium Scandinavian wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Landmannalaugar and Þórsmörk are only accessible by 4WD super jeep in winter — standard vehicles cannot reach these areas. Pre-book a reputable highland super jeep operator. The natural hot spring pool at Landmannalaugar has no facilities — bring a changing robe and dry towel.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final full morning in South Iceland. Enjoy a long, indulgent breakfast. Take a private guided walk along the South Coast cliffs near your hotel — dramatic winter scenery with crashing Atlantic waves, coastal bird life (including wintering sea birds), and potential whale spouts offshore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Blue Lagoon for a second, more indulgent visit — this time book the exclusive Retreat Spa, the most premium experience at the lagoon. The Retreat features a private in-water suite, personalized skincare treatments, exclusive access to the Retreat Lagoon (separate from the public lagoon), and a meal at the LAVA Restaurant overlooking the geothermal waters.
day_by_day.evening: Private luxury transfer to Reykjavik. Check into a premium Reykjavik hotel (e.g., The Retreat at Blue Lagoon Hotel or ION Adventure Hotel) for the final night. Farewell dinner at one of Reykjavik's finest restaurants. Final aurora watch from the city outskirts or hotel grounds.

meals.breakfast: Extended luxury farewell breakfast at South Iceland Boutique Stay — full spread with champagne toast
meals.lunch: LAVA Restaurant at Blue Lagoon — Michelin-quality Icelandic cuisine with panoramic lagoon views; seafood platter, lamb, and skyr dessert
meals.dinner: Ox Restaurant, Reykjavik — exclusive 8-seat tasting menu by Chef Þráinn Freyr Vigfússon; one of Iceland's most exclusive dining experiences with premium wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: The Retreat Spa at Blue Lagoon is the most exclusive and expensive offering — book months in advance. Ox Restaurant has very limited seating and requires advance reservation. Check out of South Iceland Boutique Stay and arrange luggage transfer to Reykjavik.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Reykjavik. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at your Reykjavik hotel. Last-minute premium shopping on Laugavegur — pick up Icelandic wool products, artisan chocolates (Omnom Chocolate), premium smoked fish, and Icelandic spirits (Brennivín, Flóki Whisky) as gifts and souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to Keflavik International Airport (45 minutes from Reykjavik). Access the airport's premium lounge. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of geothermal wonders, glacial adventures, and the ethereal magic of the Northern Lights.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight. Carry the memories of Iceland's raw, volcanic beauty, world-class hot springs, and the unforgettable green and purple curtains of the aurora borealis dancing across the Arctic sky.

meals.breakfast: Premium hotel breakfast in Reykjavik — full Nordic spread with smoked salmon, artisan cheeses, fresh pastries, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Snacks and refreshments at Keflavik Airport premium lounge or a final quick lunch at Messinn Restaurant in Reykjavik (famous for cast iron pan-fried fish)
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or airport lounge dinner

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5 hours before departure for check-in and security at Keflavik. The airport has good duty-free shopping for last-minute Icelandic spirits, chocolates, and skincare products (including Blue Lagoon skincare line). Confirm private transfer timing with your concierge the night before.
